clue.text: A former film studio (Universal) used in publicity for extreme sport

indicators.note: the studio letters are placed inside the word for publicity, as if used within it

parts.note: PR stands for public relations, i.e. publicity
RKO was a Hollywood studio that closed in the 1950s
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing

explanation.surface: An old Hollywood studio lending its name to promote a daredevil sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Universal' looks like another studio's name beside RKO, but it only supplies U.
explanation.definitionFit: Free running across urban obstacles is a daring discipline classed among extreme sports.

clue.text: Churchman with no power over dispute

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for power

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the word no is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a tiff is a minor quarrel

explanation.surface: A cleric stripped of power after a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no power' reads as a phrase meaning powerless, but 'no' is reversed by 'over' and P comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pope, the bishop of Rome, is the supreme churchman and bridge-builder of tradition.

clue.text: Scripture upheld established practices

parts.note: RI, religious instruction, is the school subject also called scripture

indicators.note: in a down clue, held up means the word for established is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: set means fixed or established

explanation.surface: Religious teaching has maintained long-standing customs.
explanation.walkthrough: RI (religious instruction) was the British school name for scripture lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceremonial observances are customary practices, especially religious ones.

clue.text: Cunning hero wins Portugal title

indicators.note: something cunning is artfully devised, so the letters of hero wins are artfully rearranged

parts.note: P is the international vehicle registration code for Portugal

explanation.surface: A crafty footballer secures a championship for Portugal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cunning' rearranges HERO WINS to OWNERSHI; P is added after.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, title means the legal right of possession to a property.

clue.text: Have sex in Australian base

definitions.meaning: in Australian slang, to ... means to have sexual intercourse
a base is the foundation or origin from which something grows

explanation.surface: Seemingly an awkward phrasebook entry on Australian sex and a home base.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian slang uses the verb for coupling, while the noun means a source or foundation.

clue.text: Failure to remember men lost in Far East

indicators.note: the jumbled men are placed in the region word

parts.note: Asia is the continent containing the Far East

indicators.note: lost suggests the letters of men have gone astray and are disordered

explanation.surface: Soldiers missing in the Orient can no longer recall anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' looks like it describes the missing men, but it is the anagram signal; 'Far East' stands for the whole continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Loss of memory, from Greek for forgetfulness, is a failure to recall.

clue.text: Made short work of …

parts.note: the idiom means dealt with quickly, but read literally it means made a written work shorter

explanation.surface: Dealt with something swiftly, trailing into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for dispatching something quickly hides its literal sense: a written work that has been shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut-down book or text is one that has been shortened, a condensed version.

clue.text: … Cardinal, formerly a sex offender

parts.note: N, north, is one of the cardinal points of the compass
once means at a former time

explanation.surface: Continuing 5, a cardinal of the church revealed as a past abuser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' suggests a churchman, but it is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: British prison and street slang for a paedophile or other sexual criminal.

clue.text: Prime commando unit outside city on June 6th

indicators.note: the unit's letters go outside the rest, wrapping round them

parts.note: the SAS is the British Special Air Service regiment
LA is Los Angeles
D-Day, the Normandy landings, was 6 June 1944

explanation.surface: Elite commandos surrounding a city on the anniversary of the Normandy landings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prime' means one's heyday, a noun, not first-rate; 'on' merely joins the date to the city.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase from Shakespeare means youthful heyday, one's best or most vigorous period.

clue.text: Stewed lamb, say, is awful

indicators.note: stewed meat is cooked down and broken up, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dish of stewed lamb, for example, tastes terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean extremely bad, dreadful in quality.

clue.text: Reportedly riding someone else's elephant? No way!

definitions.meaning: ... the Elephant is a British children's song, so sitting on another person's ... is what the phrase seems to say
an emphatic refusal, meaning certainly not

explanation.surface: An absurd question about borrowing a pachyderm, met with flat refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nelly the Elephant' is a well-known British children's song; the phrase itself comes from rhyming slang Nelly Duff for puff (life).
explanation.definitionFit: A British idiom of emphatic refusal, equivalent to certainly not.

clue.text: See 9
Still clutching front of Sunday supplement

indicators.note: the motionless word holds the other letter within its grip

parts.note: inert means motionless, still

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone motionless gripping the Sunday newspaper's magazine section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb but is an adjective meaning motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose leaflet added to a newspaper or magazine is an extra, supplementary piece.

clue.text: P.S. Dad debauched wretched nude maiden

indicators.note: debauched means corrupted, twisted out of shape, so these letters are reordered
wretched signals the letters are in a sorry, disordered state

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A postscript about a dissolute father and an unclothed young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'debauched' turns DAD into ADD and 'wretched' turns NUDE into ENDU.
explanation.definitionFit: A postscript is an afterthought added at the end of a letter, an appended note.

clue.text: Plump little man is retiring and bashful

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word for little man is read backwards

parts.note: an elf is a small mythical being
shy means bashful

explanation.surface: A short, chubby fellow who is shy and withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring and bashful' reads as a pair of synonyms, but 'retiring' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Chubby or well-padded, having plenty of flesh on the body.

clue.text: Nurse is at scene, embracing elevated emotional states

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised up means the letters read from the bottom upwards
the words hug the letters inside them

explanation.surface: A nurse at an emergency, overwhelmed by heightened feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' takes SEISATSCE from inside the words; 'elevated' turns them upward to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Raptures and transports of delight are intense emotional states.

clue.text: Sounds like suitable party food

indicators.note: the clue says these words, when spoken, resemble the solution

parts.note: meet is an old word for suitable, and a ball is a dancing party

explanation.surface: Apparently a remark that something is ideal party fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meet' is an archaic word for fitting or proper; 'party food' looks like the definition but 'party' is the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rissole of minced beef or pork is a common savoury food.

clue.text: Cunning sort of critter's awkward around king

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit around the royal letter
awkward suggests clumsy and out of order, so the letters of critter's are mixed

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A wily creature acting clumsily around a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A deceiver or prankster is a crafty, cunning person.

clue.text: Way of working over summer period with Queen's 26

parts.note: MO is modus operandi, a way of working
BST is British Summer Time
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen, plus S from the possessive

explanation.surface: A routine across summer involving the monarch's crime gangs.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts MO above BST. 26 across is TRIAD, a Chinese crime syndicate, whose members are gangsters.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a crime syndicate, as 26 describes, are gangsters.

clue.text: Cops lose suspect in den of vice

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, not right, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Police lose a suspect in a sleazy hideout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' looks like a noun, the person the police lose, but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a sewage pit is a place of corruption and vice.

clue.text: Limit most of country's spending power

parts.note: a cap is an upper limit

indicators.note: most of a word is all of it but the final letter

parts.note: Italy is a European country

explanation.surface: Restricting a nation's budget allowance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the last letter of ITALY to give ITAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Money available for investment and outlay is wealth one can spend.

clue.text: Joint publication provides absorbing material

parts.note: a T is a T-shaped pipe joint
an issue is an edition of a periodical

explanation.surface: A co-authored publication proves gripping reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbing' suggests engrossing reading, but it means soaking up liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft paper used to soak up spills is literally material that absorbs.

clue.text: Deacon has hinted regularly about upgrade

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the picked letters are read backwards
regularly picks letters at even intervals through the words

explanation.surface: A deacon has dropped hints about a promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes every second letter, ECNAHNE, and 'about' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To improve or raise the quality of something is to upgrade it.

clue.text: Most rudimentary means of transport contains one empty seat

indicators.note: the vehicle word holds the numeral inside it

parts.note: a plane is an aircraft
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: an empty word has its inside removed, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: The most basic aircraft has a single vacant seat.
explanation.definitionFit: Simplest and least elaborate, the superlative of plain, meaning most basic.

clue.text: Gangrene initially appearing in undressed elbow

indicators.note: the letter appears inside the word for undressed

parts.note: nude means undressed

indicators.note: initially means at the start, taking the opening letter

explanation.surface: A grim medical note about gangrene showing on a bare elbow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elbow' is a verb here, not the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to elbow is to jostle or prod someone with the arm.

clue.text: Outline direction to be followed by ship

parts.note: S is south, a compass direction
a ketch is a two-masted sailing vessel

explanation.surface: Instructions to a crew about following a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough drawing or summary gives the outline of something.

clue.text: Exercise skill returning home

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word for skill reads in reverse

parts.note: art means skill, as in the art of persuasion
in means at home

explanation.surface: Practising a craft on coming back home.
explanation.definitionFit: To drill or work out regularly in order to improve is to exercise.

clue.text: Contents of book? Bull about alien!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the abbreviation goes around the alien

parts.note: BS is short for bullshit, i.e. nonsense or bull
ET is the alien of the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at a book's tale of an alien as nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'book' is a bookmaker's record of wagers, not a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookmaker's book records the wagers placed with them.

clue.text: Unfinished business involving international crime syndicate

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the shortened word holds the letter
unfinished means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: trade means business, commerce

explanation.surface: Incomplete dealings drawing in a global gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' cuts TRADE to TRAD, which then takes in I.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chinese criminal secret society is a kind of organised crime syndicate.

clue.text: Trouble focusing? Yes, retina is damaged

indicators.note: damaged letters are broken and set in a new order

explanation.surface: A patient confirms their sight trouble comes from a damaged retina.
explanation.definitionFit: Tired, aching eyes from overuse make it hard to see clearly or concentrate on detail.

clue.text: Cuts classes, it's said

indicators.note: it's said signals that the word for classes is spoken, giving a word of like sound

parts.note: lessons are classes at school

explanation.surface: A student skips school, or so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuts classes' looks like truancy; 'Cuts' is a verb meaning reduces.
explanation.definitionFit: To reduce or diminish something is to cut it down.

clue.text: Peculiar variety found on borders of Somerset

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after, so this piece follows the borders
the borders of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: a range is a variety, as in a wide range

explanation.surface: An odd species discovered at the edges of an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Somerset is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean odd, unusual or out of the ordinary.
